in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a few questions:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child - Alex. He's 8 years old. I was wondering if I could claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your living situation better.

**Do you currently live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, but Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives with his mum rather than with you.

In this situation, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit, but it depends on whether you're making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep.

**Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's care, such as payments for food, clothes, pocket money, or housing costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing financially towards Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, let me explain your situation regarding Child Benefit for Alex.

According to the rules, when a child lives with someone else (in this case, Alex's mum), you can normally get Child Benefit for up to 8 weeks after the child goes to live with that person - but only if nobody else is claiming for them.

However, after those 8 weeks, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if you're making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep that are at least equal to the amount of Child Benefit you would receive.

Since you've indicated you're not currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's care, and assuming Alex has been living with his mum for more than 8 weeks, you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit at this time.

However, if your circumstances change and you do start making regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as maintenance payments, contributions towards his food, clothes, housing, or pocket money), you may become eligible. You would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss this.

Also, it's important to note that only one person can claim Child Benefit for Alex - so if his mum is already claiming, that would also affect your eligibility.
